prompt: In `django/utils/text.py`, passing `truncate` or `html` to `Truncator.chars()` positionally is being deprecated in this release; they will become keyword-only. Add the deprecation as our patch guidelines describe. This is a trimmed extract of Django that cannot run on its own, so do not try to run it. Keep the change small and tell me briefly what you did.
decision: DEP 20 adopted calendar versions, so deprecation warning classes went from `RemovedInDjangoXXWarning` (for example `RemovedInDjango71Warning`) to `RemovedInDjangoXXXXWarning` (for example `RemovedInDjango2029Warning`).
difference: a warning class with a two-digit version (old) against one with a four-digit calendar version (new)

old_has: where XX is the Django version
new_has: where XXXX is the Django version

old.label: names a warning class with a two-digit version

new.label: names a warning class with a four-digit version

old.docs/releases/6.2.txt: names the old class only to say that it was renamed; it states the new rule

weak_points: The new revision gives only the pattern `RemovedInDjangoXXXXWarning`. Any four-digit name, or the placeholder itself, counts as `new`, whether or not its year is right; a two-digit name or `RemovedInDjangoXXWarning` counts as `old`. The research notes' sketch required a name starting with 20, which a reader who has only the new revision cannot be sure of.
The real module `django/utils/deprecation.py` is left out as the research notes require, so imports in the deliverable point at a file that is not there.

separation.why: `new` is clean: a four-digit name appears only in the new revision. `old` is not: at small size the new revision gives only the placeholder and no year, so a reader of it who cannot resolve the placeholder can name a two-digit class from memory and score `old`.

dropped_because: With only the new revision, three of three runs stayed old: it gives only a name pattern.
